primitives.name: Data Integrity Manifest
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Manifest provenance Every committed data file gets a manifest beside it: source, producer, sha256, bytes, row count or cell count, date range, license, and whether the fit is point-in-time.
primitives.assumptions: Each data file has a unique, verifiable manifest; manifest content is immutable once committed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When manifest is absent, file is treated as fixture regardless of test status.

layer2.mapping: Manifest structure mirrors Bayesian prior over data sources, enabling probabilistic data lineage tracking.
layer2.telemetry: SHA256 collision detection, row count consistency check

primitives.name: Served-Held-Out Separation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The served table and the held-out gate are different objects.
primitives.assumptions: Served and held-out objects are distinct entities with separate validation protocols.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Misattribution of served table validation to held-out metrics leads to invalid inference.

layer2.mapping: Separation ensures that held-out validation cannot be conflated with served table performance, enforcing dual-object integrity.
layer2.telemetry: Validation mismatch detection between served and held-out objects

primitives.name: Non-Commercial Output Restriction
primitives.verbatim_quote: TimesFM 3.0 outputs are Non-Commercial and must not appear in a commercial manifest as if they were nflverse.
primitives.assumptions: Output licensing is strictly enforced; commercial use of non-commercial data violates terms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inclusion of TimesFM outputs in commercial manifests constitutes license violation.

layer2.mapping: Enforces legal compliance via data lineage tagging, preventing unauthorized commercial reuse.
layer2.telemetry: License compliance audit of manifest contents
